# 4 Ezra Chapter 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 4:2 — Uriel's opening challenge

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Your heart has utterly-failed in-regard-to this world" | Literal hyphenated |
| LOGOS | "Your heart has utterly failed in its understanding of this world" | Adds implied object |
| PNEUMA | "Your understanding has completely broken down even in this world" | Restructures freely |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Your heart has utterly failed in understanding this world" — LOGOS's expansion improves clarity without major departure.

---

## 4:4 — "evil heart" provenance

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "whence the evil heart-proceeds" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "from where the evil heart proceeds" | Standard English order |
| PNEUMA | "where this evil heart of ours actually comes from" | Adds "of ours" — interpretive but accurate |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "From where the evil heart proceeds" (LOGOS). The addition of "of ours" by PNEUMA, while theologically astute (cor malignum is humanity's shared problem), goes beyond the Latin.

---

## 4:12 — "better not to exist" lament

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "It-were-better that-we were-not-here at-all" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "It were better that we had not come here at all" | Slightly stronger — "had not come" |
| PNEUMA | "It would have been better if we'd never been born at all" | "Never been born" is more vivid but slightly beyond the Latin |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "It were better that we had never come here at all" — blends LOGOS (stronger past) with EMET's "never."

---

## 4:28 — cor malignum (evil heart/inclination)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "grain of evil-seed" | Literal Latin granum seminis mali |
| LOGOS | "grain of evil seed" | Same without hyphen |
| PNEUMA | "seed of evil" | Slightly compressed |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Grain of evil seed" (LOGOS). The full phrase preserves the agricultural metaphor running through the chapter.

---

## 4:37 — pregnant woman simile

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as the pregnant-woman in-the-ninth-month, when-the-hour-of-her-delivery-draws-near her womb is-pained" | Full literal with hyphens |
| LOGOS | "as a pregnant woman in the ninth month, when the hour of her delivery draws near, feels her womb ache" | Natural English |
| PNEUMA | "Like a woman nine months pregnant whose labor pains begin as delivery approaches" | Restated naturally |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "As a pregnant woman in the ninth month, when the hour of her delivery draws near, feels her womb ache" (LOGOS). The most precise rendering.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
